import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 484

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/484](https://www.erdosproblems.com/484)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [ESS89] Erdős, P., Sárközy, A., and Sós, V. T., *On a conjecture of Roth and some related
  problems. I*. (1989), 47-59.
-/

namespace Erdos484

open scoped Classical in
/--
Prove that there exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, whenever $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is
$k$-coloured (and $N$ is large enough depending on $k$) then there are at least $cN$ many
integers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ which are representable as a monochromatic sum (that is, $a+b$
where $a,b\in \{1,\ldots,N\}$ are in the same colour class and $a\neq b$).

A conjecture of Roth. Solved by Erdős, Sárközy, and Sós [ESS89], who in fact prove that
there are at least $\frac{N}{2}-O(N^{1-1/2^{k+1}})$ many even numbers which are of this form.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos484.lean"]
theorem erdos_484 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N → ∀ f : ℕ → Fin k,
      c * N ≤ (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter fun n =>
        ∃ a ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∃ b ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
          a ≠ b ∧ f a = f b ∧ a + b = n).card : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos484

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement colours all of ℕ and uses N₀ ≤ N and cN ≤ count. The original formulations in [Er61] and [Er80] colour the finite interval and use n > n₀ and count > cn.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For k > 0, every interval colouring extends to ℕ by assigning a fixed colour outside the interval, and every global colouring restricts to the interval. The counted set is unchanged because both summands lie in [1,N]. A weak lower bound with constant c gives a strict lower bound with constant c/2 for positive N. Conversely, a strict lower bound implies the weak one, and increasing the threshold by one handles the different threshold convention. The full equivalence, including the quantifier order, was proved as Review484.global_iff_source_strict_local in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the sorry-backed problem theorem.

review.notes: No mathematical defects found. The uniform constant, threshold dependence, distinctness requirement, and counting of target integers rather than representations agree with the primary sources. Lean checks covered N = 0, 1, 2, one-colour examples, parity colouring, and an injective finite colouring. The linked proof compiled with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. A separately kernel-checked bridge shows that its floor-valued bound implies the exact repository statement by halving the constant and enlarging the threshold, supporting both recorded annotations. The current erdosproblems.com page was inaccessible because of Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the comparison instead used all three cited primary papers. All experiments are under /workspace/review/; the reviewed file was verified identical to HEAD.
